title: Ecosystem channel listing kickoff notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the working kickoff kit for launching a partner listing into cloud vendor marketplaces and partner portals. It's intentionally pragmatic: sequence of tasks, minimum acceptable copy, gating criteria, basic QA matrix, and quick fallback plans. 

Goal for this sprint (MVP):
- Have a validated, vendor-ready listing bundle + metadata + 1-sku mapping for AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace pilot by end of next sprint (target date: 2024-11-20)
- Clear owner for each gate so we can sign off quickly

Primary audience: GTM launch PM, partner success lead, partner engineering, legal/finance reviewer, partner ops vendor contact.

High-level constraints/assumptions (read before editing):
- We will submit using vendor portals; some fields are non-negotiable (billing SKU, legal terms, regional availability).
- Start with EN-US only; plan + checklist for l10n after staging pass.
- Use Redwood-hosted docs links (public) and a private hub for partner artifacts.

Kickoff playlist (sequential tasks, rough estimates):
1) Asset intake (2 days) — owner: Partner Ops (Priya)
   - Required: product one-liner, 50/150/450 char descriptions, 3 screenshots (1920x1080), 1 short explainer video (<=60s), logo SVG + PNG
   - Gate: all assets present and PNG/SVG pass automated size checks

2) Draft marketplace copy + persona variants (3 days) — owner: Product Marketing (Maya)
   - Deliverables: Title (max char per vendor), short blurb (50 chars), 150-char summary, 450-char long description, 3 benefit bullets, 2 customer quotes (placeholders ok)
   - Gate: internal content review sign-off from PM and Sales Engineering

3) Technical listing fields & SKU mapping (1 day) — owner: Partner Engineering (Samir)
   - Deliverables: billing SKU, entitlements (compute/storage), region availability, minimum instance type guidance, required tags for our telemetry
   - Gate: Finance + Billing confirm SKU mapping and pricing tier; Product accepts instance guidance

4) Compliance & legal quick-check (2 days) — owner: Legal (Nora)
   - Deliverables: T&Cs mapping doc, data handling summary, export controls checklist, privacy FAQ snippet
   - Gate: Legal provides redlines or explicit approval for vendor terms

5) Portal submission + vendor QA (3 days) — owner: Partner Ops + vendor rep
   - Deliverables: Completed portal form, contact for vendor reviewer, expected review SLA, screenshot of preview page
   - Gate: Portal preview approved by PM and Partner Ops

6) Staging acceptance tests (2 days) — owner: SRE/Partner Eng
   - Tests: install flow, auth with keys, sample inference call, perf sanity (p90 < 500ms for 32-token request target env), billing event test (mock purchase)
   - Gate: all tests pass in vendor staging and smoke checklist is green

7) Go/no-go + launch play (1 day) — owner: GTM Launch PM
   - Deliverables: Launch checklist signoff, announcement plan, partner enablement doc link
   - Gate: all above steps signed off; fallback plan documented

Minimum acceptable listing copy (MVP block):
- Title (for vendor storefront): Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM inference platform
- 50-char blurb: Fast, predictable LLM inference for production apps
- 150-char summary: Deliver consistent low-latency inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ideal for product teams that need predictable performance and cost controls.
- 450-char long description (draft): Redwood Inference provides a production-grade inference platform that helps engineering teams ship LLM features with predictable latency, lower per-token costs, and enterprise-ready controls. Use hosted APIs for rapid development, dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or a private deployment for regulated workloads. Features include real-time streaming, model rollouts, cost-aware batching, and observability for token-level diagnostics.
- 3 benefit bullets (single-sentence):
  • Reduce inference costs with smart batching & KV caching
  • Maintain performance targets via dedicated GPU pools and SLO-backed routing
  • Keep data secure with VPC/private control plane options and KMS integrations

Persona microcopy variants (useful for vendor filters/industry targeting):
- For startups/PLG: "Get started with a predictable API — free credits and a quick SDK to prototype."
- For enterprise/security-conscious: "Bring Redwood into your VPC or on-prem for full control and audit logs."
- For platform teams: "Standardize inference across teams with rollout policies, tracing, and cost breakdowns."

Quality acceptance matrix (staging):
- Asset check: images render and alt text present (pass/fail)
- Copy check: length limits satisfied, no prohibited words per vendor policy (pass/fail)
- Functional test: sample API call returns 200 and valid tokens (pass/fail)
- Billing test: SKU creation > test purchase event generated and recorded in our ledger (pass/fail)
- Perf sanity: p90 <= target (pass/fail)
- Security quick check: no hard-coded keys in artifact; KMS reference present (pass/fail)

Common deal-breakers (escalate immediately):
- Vendor requires commitments incompatible with our hosted model (e.g., forced revenue share or lock-in clauses we can't accept)
- Vendor requires data residency changes that conflict with existing customer SLAs
- Legal asks for an indemnity clause wider than standard (route to Legal for escalation)

Rollback / fallback plan (if listing blocked post-approval):
- Unpublish listing + notify partners via partner ops channel
- Revert copy to previous approved draft and resubmit with follow-up ticket to vendor support
- If billing SKU problem: remove purchasable SKU and keep free trial/information-only listing while finance resolves mapping

Localization notes (later sprint):
- After EN-US is live: localize title + 150-char summary for DE/FR/JP with a native copywriter; avoid machine-only translation for legal fields
- Capture localized screenshots and local pricing tiers where vendor SDK supports it

Open questions / TODOs (placeholders for next sync):
- Confirm our expected review SLA with AWS marketplace rep (Priya is chasing; ref: slack thread)
- Who will provide a verified customer quote for the listing? Sales to supply or use anonymized case study?
- Pricing model: do we use per-token metering or tiered monthly seat model for the pilot? Finance input needed (Samir flagged)

Meeting notes snapshot (2024-10-25 internal kickoff):
- Quick decisions: start EN-US only; use per-token metering for hosted SKU in pilot; dedicated SKU will be informational only for first pass
- Action owners assigned inline above; weekly sync Tuesdays 11am PT (recurring invite)

Next immediate actions (this week):
- Priya: collect all assets from partner and upload to shared drive (due 2024-10-18)
- Maya: finalize MVP copy and share for PM/SE review (due 2024-10-17)
- Samir: confirm SKU mapping and billing test plan with finance (due 2024-10-19)
- Nora: run quick legal surface review and flag any auto-reject clauses (due 2024-10-20)

Notes / style guidance for copywriter (PMM):
- Tone: engineer-forward, concise, benefit-led. Avoid marketing fluff (no "revolutionary" or "disruptive").
- Metrics: where possible include concrete numbers (e.g., "reduce token cost by up to X%" only with measurement backing). Otherwise use qualitative phrasing ("lower per-token costs").
- Allowed logos: partner logos only with signed logo use agreement (link to contract in linked_artifacts)

Version history (quick):
- 2024-10-15: initial draft (Maya)
- 2024-10-18: asset intake section updated (Priya)
- 2024-11-01: added staging QA matrix and rollback plan (Samir)

End of doc — this is intentionally a living doc. Use inline comments and update status when a gate is complete.

Quick pointer: Preview checklist template will be copied to Confluence as "GTM Marketplace Launch Template" — link above.
